question.prompt: If the perimeter of rectangle \(ABCD\) is \(20\) inches, the least value of diagonal \(AC,\) in inches, is:

solutions.explanation:
The perimeter fixes the sum of two adjacent sides. Let \(AB=u\) and \(BC=v\), measured in inches. Since both side lengths are positive,
\[
2(u+v)=20,
\qquad v=10-u,
\qquad 0<u<10.
\]
The diagonal is the hypotenuse of right triangle \(ABC\), so the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
AC^2&=u^2+(10-u)^2\\
&=2u^2-20u+100\\
&=2(u-5)^2+50.
\end{aligned}
\]
Writing the expression as a square plus a constant reveals its minimum. Because \((u-5)^2\ge0\), we have \(AC^2\ge50\). Equality holds when \(u=5\), which gives \(v=5\). This square has perimeter \(20\), so the bound is attained. Taking the positive square root, the least diagonal is \(\boxed{\sqrt{50}}\) inches, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Minimize the squared diagonal
Maximize the side product by AM-GM
